newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bourse weaker in thin market awaiting a spur.
newsitem.headline: Irish bourse weaker in thin market awaiting a spur.

text.p: The Irish equity market drifted off in thin trade caused by the closure of the UK because of a national holiday, dealers said.
"It's almost like a day off. We're getting on with our paperwork," one equity dealer said.
Dealers said London's closure meant it had yet to react to a fall in Wall Street on Friday and weakness in the Dow on Monday afternoon, where it was off 22 points by 1530 GMT.
"There's still a day's catch-up to do so we'll see how London performs when it opens tomorrow," another dealer said.
By 1530 GMT the ISEQ index was down to 2521.42 from a Friday close of 2532.25.
Dealers said the frontline AIB and BOI stocks were both off a penny but said the movement was exaggerated by the thinness of the market.
Jurys Hotels was quoted at 280 pence from close of 277 on Friday after its annual general meeting on Monday at which CEO Peter Malone was upbeat about 1996 prospects.
He said Jurys had gained from its exposure to the strong Irish economy through its corporate and commercial business, tourism, event-related activity and weekend business breaks.
"It looks good at that price and could move some more upwards then the market proper returns," a dealer said.
